# Sources

The patch idiom library describes techniques. Techniques and facts are
not anybody's property, and the descriptions here are our own words --
nothing is transcribed from any of the works below. This page records
what informed the work, and is honest about how much.

Of **97** idioms: **14** were written from, or checked against, a text we hold and quote; **83** were written from general knowledge of the practice; **0** were reasoned out from adjacent technique. That first number is the only one under which a work can honestly be listed as a source, and it is the smaller number on purpose.

## Derived from

Each idiom below cites a passage, and a check confirms the citation
quotes text that is really there. A citation that stops verifying is
moved out of this section automatically.

- ARP 2600 — the instrument, and the practice that grew around it
  — `ensemble-vibrato`, `gliding-intervals`, `marimba-roll`
- Fred Welsh, *Welsh's Synthesizer Cookbook*
  — `portamento`
- Gordon Reid, *Synth Secrets* (Sound On Sound, 1999–2004)
  — `body-resonance-bank`, `fixed-modulator-am`, `glissando`, `growl`, `tracking-modulator-am`
- Kim Bjørn & Chris Meyer, *Patch & Tweak* (Bjooks)
  — `attenuverted-modulation`, `quantized-voice`, `ring-modulated-texture`, `sequential-switch-routing`, `west-coast-voice`

## In the tradition of

These works describe the practice this library is built on. We have
not verified a passage for the idioms below, and several of these
works we could not obtain in a readable form at all; naming them is
acknowledgement, not citation.

- Allen Strange, *Electronic Music: Systems, Techniques and Controls* — 32 idioms
- ARP 2600 — the instrument, and the practice that grew around it — 6 idioms
- Kim Bjørn & Chris Meyer, *Patch & Tweak* (Bjooks) — 2 idioms
- Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois — the shimmer technique — 1 idiom
- Curtis Roads, *The Computer Music Tutorial* — 1 idiom
- Godfried Toussaint's work on Euclidean rhythms — 1 idiom
- John Chowning's work on frequency modulation — 1 idiom
- Karplus and Strong's plucked-string algorithm — 1 idiom
- Make Noise — the Maths function generator and its manual — 1 idiom
- Rob Hordijk's Rungler and Benjolin — 1 idiom
- Steve Reich's phase music — 1 idiom
- The Roland TB-303, and the music made from it — 1 idiom
- Todd Barton's Krell patch, after Louis and Bebe Barron — 1 idiom
- Tom Whitwell / Music Thing Modular — the Turing Machine — 1 idiom

A further **32** idioms record standard practice with
no particular work behind them: the things every synthesist knows,
which belong to nobody.

## How this page is kept honest

It is generated from the records, by `tools/rack/notice.py`. The tier
of each record is data; the anchor that justifies a *derived from*
entry is data; the counts are counted. Editing this file by hand would
let it drift from the library, so a test fails when it is stale.
